findings.message: The round-3 fix only covers the case where the same option was already settled as `confirmed`. Any other own decision (`unknown`, `failed`, `expired`) returns false. confirmCard then records `not_chosen`, calls `cancelled()` (whose settle overwrites `decided[id]` with `cancelled`) and tells the person nothing was changed. An `unknown` outcome means the write may have run, so it is reported as a clean cancel and the stored decision is rewritten. Fix: when the option is no longer pending, return lost only when `decided[action.id]` is `cancelled` (a sibling beat it). For any other own decision, fall through so `withIdempotency` (or a fresh `lookupKey`) reports the key's real outcome. Do not settle over it. Add cases for `unknown` and `failed` to the double-confirm test.
findings.scenario: Option A is double-tapped. Attempt 2 passes `lookupKey` while attempt 1's key is not claimed yet (for example, `withAnswer` is slow). Attempt 1 then runs and settles `unknown` because nested writes made `run.nested` > 0. Attempt 2 reaches claimChoice: A is not pending and `decided[A]` is `unknown`, so it returns false. It records `not_chosen`, rewrites `decided[A]` to `cancelled`, and the person reads 'I cancelled A' although the write may have happened.

findings.message: The new same-option double-confirm test says in its own comment that it does not force the interleaving the fix is for (attempt 2 passing `lookupKey` before attempt 1 settles). It also passes without the round-3 change, so it doesn't prove the fix (B2/B7). Fix: force the order. For example, hold a lock or delay attempt 1's settle (a trigger on `core.idempotency` or `chat.conversation`, or an injected hook) until attempt 2 has passed `lookupKey`. Then assert one write, two `done` outcomes and no `not_chosen` step. Also cover the case where the first attempt's decision is `unknown`.
findings.scenario: Revert the claimChoice change in engine.ts:394 and run the test: two parallel confirms almost never land in the window, so the test stays green.
